messages:
sam_support: Heads-up — customer ACME hitting lots of 429s during a traffic spike, says Dedicated pool didn’t scale quickly. They reported ~70–90s of elevated 429s before more instances became ready. attaching the brief repro we used.
lee_oncall: :eyes: got the customer ID? any recent quota or billing blocks?
sam_support: AcmeOrg-312. Billing \/ quotas look clean. No billing holds. We ran a synthetic ramp from their side and reproduced. Quick repro (from our support lab):
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://dedicated.redwood.example/v1/generate & done
```
Observed 429s start ~10s into the ramp and kept until ~85s. Probe logs show attach / warmchain delays and probe backoffs.
hana_eng: can you paste the autoscaler logs? particularly probe/backoff and min_replicas settings.
sam_support: pasted snippets below from control-plane and node agent (timestamps removed):
```
autoscaler: desired=12 current=2 min_replicas=1 max_replicas=50 scale_up_cooldown=30s probe_backoff=4s
auth: token_valid=true
attach-manager: warmchain_ready=0/6 attach_attempts=3 attach_backoff=16s
worker: pod_start_ts=+0s image_pull=OK container_ready=+58s
```
mike_infra: looks like min_replicas=1 + warmchain probes failing = big chill. With aggressive ramp the system waits for probe_backoff windows before requesting more capacity. Also noticed registry pulls clustered, maybe noisy neighbor on registry IO.
lee_oncall: customer notes they run large model footprints which makes pod startup ~45–70s on GPU nodes. If autoscaler relies on successful warmchain probes before spinning additional nodes it can create a gap.
hana_eng: agree. two short-term mitigations: 1) bump min_replicas for their org to 3 while we stabilize; 2) reduce probe_backoff and scale_up_cooldown for dedicated tier temporarily. We should also enable preemptive warmpool for heavy models.
I'll open an infra change request.
sam_support: customer agreed to temporary min_replicas=3. Please coordinate patch. Also they asked if auth/token rotation could be contributing — confirmed no, token_valid=true in logs.
mike_infra: investigating registry pull logs now. If noisy neighbor caused spikes in image pull times we'll add jitter to concurrent pulls. Seen in cluster: many concurrent ACME and another-tenant pulls at same time.
Deploy-bot: Deployment ADJUSTMENT queued: change org.AcmeOrg-312.min_replicas -> 3 (request id TICKET-3421). Scheduled for manual window 10:15 UTC.
hana_eng: After change we'll run the same synthetic ramp and capture attach/warmchain metrics. Also adding an autoscaler metric to alert if scaled_desired - scaled_ready > 4 for >30s.
lee_oncall: plan sounds good. For long-term: consider proactive capacity hinting for orgs with large models (pre-warm). Add to roadmap item INFRA-1289.
sam_support: customer updated — after min_replicas bumped they saw 429s drop to zero within 10s of ramp, overall latency still elevated until pods fully warmed (~40–50s) but acceptable. Customer happy for now :thumbsup:
hana_eng: follow-ups: we still need to address probe_backoff logic and image pull contention. I'll put together a short RFC with options (reduce probe backoff, speculative scaling, warmpool allocation) and link to TICKET-3421 and INFRA-1289.
mike_infra: will also add a short-term registry pull-rate limiter per-tenant to smooth spikes.

--- end thread ---
